subject: Post-call: Real-time Recs POC — latency budget, throughput targets & topology options
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@realtime.co>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Real-time Recs POC — latency budget, throughput targets & topology options

Thanks again for the call today — appreciated the clear framing of the business need. Below is a concise recap of what we heard, the technical constraints you confirmed, and the options we discussed for the POC topology. Please flag anything I mis-stated.

Summary of pain/goals:
- Product goal: real-time personalized recommendations in the product detail page (RTP). Target is near-interactive UX for logged-in users.
- Primary pain: current system (microservice + lookup table) has 150-300ms tail latency hitting external feature store, causing user-visible jitter during browsing.
- Business metric: reduce recommendation render time to under 200ms perceived by user; technical SLO for model inference p95 <= 50ms end-to-end (inference-only).
- Throughput observed: average 80 qps during peak, expected to grow to 200 qps in 3 months. Bursts up to 400 qps for flash sales.

Key technical constraints you confirmed:
- Model family: you prefer an open weight conversational/encoder-decoder variant (we talked about a distilled Llama2-Chat style candidate).
- Data residency: US-only for the POC.
- Security: SOC2 + IP allowlisting; no customer data is stored outside VPC during POC.

POC topology options (tradeoffs we discussed):
1) Dedicated VPC RG (single AZ, heavy batching, aggressive KV prefix cache) — pros: lowest cost-per-token via batching/longer queues; cons: unlikely to meet p95=50ms for single-request flows.
2) Multi-AZ Dedicated (concurrent pools + warm standby, prefix/KV cache replicated) — pros: best p95 and availability for 200–400 qps; cons: higher committed capacity.
3) Hybrid: hosted control plane + private serving in your VPC with elastic burst to Redwood Dedicated — pros: quicker onboarding, fallback to hosted smaller-quantized variant; cons: cross-network latency must be measured.

Suggested baseline for POC (what Redwood will propose in the SOW):
- Target inference-only p95: 45ms (buffer under 50ms)
- Sustained throughput target: 200 qps, burst to 400 qps for 60s windows
- Model: quantized 4-bit / int8-ish optimized candidate; fallback to smaller 7B variant for extreme bursts
- Ops: prefix/KV cache on GPU cold-starts + per-team traffic steering (latency-first routing)

Immediate next steps (action owners):
- Samir (Realtime): share representative latency/trace samples and CSV of 48-hour production qps distribution (you said you can send by Monday).
- Evelyn (Redwood): draft a POC topology options matrix + rough capacity estimate for each option (we'll include expected GPUs, expected p95 under lab tests). Deliverable by Tue, 2027-06-08 EOD.
- Marcus: prepare a short checklist of SOC2/compliance items we'll need for Private/VPC onboarding.
- Connor: propose two 60-minute deep-dive slots next week to discuss batch vs. single-token latency tradeoffs and a short demo of prefix caching behavior.

Attachments: we will include a sample POC SOW and a CSV template for latency samples in the follow-up.

Thanks — talk soon.

Evelyn Hart
Senior Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Evelyn.Hart@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: Real-time Recs POC — latency budget, throughput targets & topology options

Evelyn — thanks for the clear recap. All looks right; a couple clarifications and data attached.

Clarifications:
- Our 48-hour qps distribution is spiky: median 70 qps, 95th ~210 qps, 99th ~360 qps.
- Per-request feature payload is ~1.5 KB; we currently do a 3–5 call fan-out to downstream feature stores before recommendation. We want to fold feature retrieval into the inference hop where possible.
- Data retention during POC: we can enable ephemeral caching (30m TTL) but cannot persist user PII.

Attached sample CSV: realtime_latency_samples.csv — includes measured edge-to-service and service-to-feature-store timings.

On topology: multi-AZ Dedicated (option 2) seems most realistic to meet p95 target without significant code changes on our side. We are ok with a short commitment if the cost model is reasonable.

I'll coordinate legal/procurement to do a non-prod addendum for the POC. Expect a short note from procurement mid-week with procurement contacts.

Samir
Senior Engineering Manager | Realtime Systems, Inc.
samir@realtime.co | +1 (212) 555-0134

- Connor — can you run a quick lab run against the sample CSV to sanity-check KV-cache hit ratios and give a back-of-envelope for GPU-hours? If you can share results by EOD Tue that'd help the SOW.

Proposed deep-dive times (pick one):

Evelyn
